issues.description: The problem statement's Pneumatic interface specifies a method openValve(), but the solution implementation declares releaseValve() instead. This is a direct identifier mismatch for the same conceptual operation (opening/releasing the valve) and will confuse students mapping the UML/problem requirements to the code. It may also cause failing tests or compilation issues because method names differ between the expected specification and the provided interface.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the Pneumatic interface name with the UML/problem statement. Rename releaseValve() in the Pneumatic interface to openValve(), and update all implementing classes (e.g., LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) to implement openValve(). Alternatively, if releaseValve() was intentional, update the problem statement/UML to use releaseValve() — but the preferred fix is to change the solution code to openValve() so it matches the UML and exercise description.
